subject: Performance benchmarking deep-dive / demo scheduling
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@acme.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-12T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Performance deep-dive / load test request

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — RetailX is excited about what Redwood can bring for our recommendation and search workloads. Before we move to an internal procurement conversation, our infra team has asked for a technical deep-dive focused on performance and latency benchmarking. High level ask: validate whether Redwood can meet our throughput and p95 latency targets for production traffic, and run a short load test.

Rough targets from our side:
- Aggregate sustained throughput: ~8,000 tokens/sec
- Concurrency: ~100 concurrent streams
- Typical sequence length: 256–512 tokens (many sequences are 512 during peak)
- p95 latency goal: <250ms for 512-token generation (end-to-end)

We'd like to schedule a technical session to align on test plan, infra (GPU types), warmup strategy, and run a short smoke load test. Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue Apr 14 at 10:00 AM PT
- Tue Apr 14 at 2:00 PM PT
- Wed Apr 15 at 9:00 AM PT

I'll loop in Brianna (our infra lead) who will provide dataset samples. Can you also share a short runbook and list of artifacts you need (e.g., sample queries, client concurrency harness)?

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Director of Engineering
Acme.ai

Attachments: sample_queries.json (I'll share full payloads in Drive)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@acme.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-12T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance deep-dive / load test request

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear targets, this is perfect. We'd be happy to run a focused benchmarking session + short smoke tests.

Agenda proposal (45–60m):
1) Align on workload shape and SLA targets (tokens/seq, concurrency, p95 goals)
2) Test infra & constraints (GPU type, model variant, quantization)
3) Runbook walkthrough and what we'll collect (latency percentiles, token/sec, error rates, system metrics)
4) Quick smoke run (15–20m) and follow-ups

We can do Tue Apr 14 at 10:00 AM PT — that works for our team. I'm attaching our initial runbook (load_test_plan.xlsx) and an example perf output (perf_results_sample.csv) so you have visibility into what we collect. Can Brianna share a small (~200 sample) query set and an estimate of your expected peak token mix (ratio short:long sequences)?

Notes for the run:
- We'll bring both A100 80GB and H100 80GB backends when relevant; we'll default to the model variant you used in the demo unless you request another.
- We'll do a 10–15 minute warmup before the smoke run to prime KV caches and JIT kernels.
- We'll measure p50/p90/p95/p99 and report token throughput and cost estimates.

Proposed calendar invite: https://meet.google.com/xyz-abc-def (I'll send a formal invite once everyone confirms).

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, alice@acme.ai
Date: 2026-04-12T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance deep-dive / load test request

Hey all — quick heads-up: I have a conflict at 10am PT on Apr 14. Can we shift to 2pm PT that day? If not, I can join remotely for the smoke run portion only.

Technical notes for Alice/Brianna so we can prepare:
- Please confirm which model and quantization you want tested (FP16 vs int8/4-bit). Int8/4-bit results vary depending on token mix and sequence length.
- For accurate production-like results, share your expected request rate distribution (e.g., 70% <64 tokens, 20% 64–256, 10% 256–512).
- We'll do parallel runs across hardware types (A100/H100) and include a config for aggressive batching vs. latency-optimized single-request path.

If we do 2pm PT, we can also attempt a longer load window (30 min) to validate autoscaling behavior and cache hit rates.

Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Tue, Apr 12, 2026 at 11:30 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alice — thanks for the clear targets, this is perfect. We'd be happy to run a focused benchmarking session + short smoke tests....

From: Brianna Torres <brianna@retailx.com>

Cc: Alice Chen <alice@acme.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-13T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance deep-dive / load test request

Hi Soojin / Marcus — thanks for the options. We actually prefer Apr 14 at 10:00 AM PT (earlier slot) due to internal scheduling. Marcus, if you can't make the whole session, being present for the smoke run is fine.

Dataset & traffic shape:
- We'll share a 200-sample query set (mix attached in Drive). Many of our peak queries are ~512 tokens but the median is ~120.
- Expected distribution: ~65% <128 tokens, ~25% 128–512, ~10% >512.
- Typical concurrency during peak is 80–120 steady streams; bursts up to ~200 for short windows.

We'd like the smoke run to validate: overall token throughput, p95 latency at 512 tokens, and error/failure modes under burst. We'll post the Drive link with sample inputs by today: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C

Thanks — Brianna
Infrastructure Lead, RetailX

Attachment: sample_query_summary.txt (in Drive)

Meeting: Performance deep-dive & smoke load test
When: 2026-04-14 10:00 AM PT (60m)
Location: https://meet.google.com/xyz-abc-def

Pre-call actions (owners):
- RetailX (Brianna): share 200-sample query set and typical token distribution in Drive (done)
- Redwood (Soojin / Marcus): review runbook and confirm target model + quantization by EOD today
- Redwood (Marissa / David): prepare short dashboard showing p50/p90/p95/p99 and token/sec counters for the smoke run

Test notes:

- Smoke run: 15–20m steady load targeting ~8k tokens/sec aggregate with concurrency window of 80–120
- Metrics: per-request latency, token throughput, error rate, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates

Attachments included on the calendar event: load_test_plan.xlsx, perf_results_sample.csv, architecture_diagram.pdf

If anyone needs the invite moved, please reply with alternatives — otherwise we'll see you all tomorrow at 10.
